Port Watch Arrivals #103 A hall built to process people and not quite wide enough to do it. A customs counter runs along the north wall under the Port Watch's crest, a rayed circle over a wave, with a brass rail polished by elbows. Across from it a notice wall carries the port's rules in Freeport Council type and, around and over them, cooperative notices three layers deep. The light is warm and a little yellow, the only warm light on the deck. The air smells of printer heat and the coffee on the counter's far end. Voices carry; a stair behind a glass door goes down to the freight deck, and the concourse opens east. Registry & Co-op Desk #105 Two counters share one room and do not share a style. Freeport Concourse #104 The widest space on the deck and the loudest: boots on plate, a tannoy that clears its throat every few minutes, the Exchange ticker crawling along the east arch. Overhead the lighting is bright, bluish and new, bolted to a ceiling that is neither. A backlit map of the port stands in the middle on a pedestal with a directory under it, and benches around it hold crews waiting for clearances, for pay, for each other. The air smells of too many people and the sweet-metal tang of recycled water. Doors lead north to the Clearing and south to the Slack Line; Arrivals is west, the Exchange east. Exchange Hall #107 A long hall under a price board that fills the whole north wall, white figures on black: metal concentrate by the tonne under the Exchange's mark, volatiles and reaction mass under the Occator drop-and-flame, an alloy bid in a column of its own, and a line of dashes where a Pallas consignment used to be. A counter runs the length of the hall below it, brass-railed, with the factor's stamp pads and manifest slots at intervals. The floor is damp near the east end, where a sample tap drips into a grating, and the whole room smells of wet steel and the faint sweetness of electrolysed water. A roller door at that end is stencilled FREIGHT STAIR, BERTH HOLDERS, and is shut. Doors lead north to Tycho and south to the chandlery; the concourse is west. #126 Rosalind Qureshi-Mbeki#127 Margit Søndergaard-Achebe Concourse <W> wwestconcourseChandlery <S> ssouthchandlerystoresTycho <N> nnorthtychoagency autumn afternoon

Co-op Chandlery #108 Shelving to the ceiling on three sides, stacked with grey cases stencilled PROVISIONS / 10 CREW-DAYS and the Co-op's linked hands, and a cage at the back where the counted stock lives. Pressure Lobby #102 A square of scuffed deck between two sets of pressure doors, lit flat and white, with nothing in it that would matter if the doors had to close.
